text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Songwriter STEPHEN FOSTER was born in 1826. Among his more popular works were "Swanee River", "Beautiful Dreamer" and "Old Folks at Home".
Irish philanthropist, THOMAS BARNARDO, who founded homes for destitute children, was born in 1845.
LOUIS B. MAYER, U.S. film producer, was born in Russia in 1885. Along with with SAMUEL GOLDWYN, he formed the MGM studios and guided it through the "golden age" of cinema in the U.S.
Jazz star LOUIS ARMSTRONG, who was known as the great "Satchmo", was born in 1900. His combination of sweet trumpet and raspy voice made him a popular performer for more than 50 years.

American orchestra leader and producer, MITCH MILLER, who made a name for himself with 'Sing Along with Mitch' albums and television programmes, was born in 1911. Hits with his own orchestra included "Yellow Rose of Texas" (1955) and "River Kwai March" (1958). He produced artists such as TONY BENNETT, JOHNNY MATHIS, FRANK SINATRA, FRANKIE LANE and PERCY FAITH'S orchestra.
American singer, guitarist and songwriter, BILL WITHERS, was born in 1938. Hits included "Ain't No Sunshine"(1971), "Lean On Me"(1972), "Use Me"(1972) and "Just the Two of Us"(1981).

British singer/songwriter, JEREMY SPENCER, who was a founding member of 'Fleetwood Mac', was born in 1948. In February 1971 he told the other band members in a Los Angeles hotel room that he was popping out for a minute. He wasn't seen for two years. He joined the Children of God sect and in 1973 released an album called "Jeremy Spencer and the Children of God."
American drummer with 'Earth, Wind and Fire', RALPH JOHNSON, was born in 1951.
** EVENTS **
1190 : RICHARD I of England and PHILIP II of France
started on the Third Crusade.
1631 : The world's first employment agency opened in
Paris.
1776 : The American Declaration of Independence was
signed.
1826 : THOMAS JEFFERSON, third U.S. president (1801-09),
and JOHN ADAMS, second president (1797-1801), both died on this day.
1829 : The first horse drawn buses went into service in
London.
1831 : JAMES MONROE, fifth U.S. president (1817-25),
died. In 1823 he introduced the Monroe Doctrine, which committed the U.S. to a Western Hemisphere safe from aggression.
1848 : The Communist Manifesto, written by Karl Marx and
Friedrich Engels, was published.
1853 : Outspoken women's rights campaigner, AMELIA
BLOOMER, shocked her Connecticut audience by delivering her speech while wearing trousers. She spoke against the requirement for women to cover their legs. Mrs BLOOMER wore a knee-length

skirt over loose-fitting trousers bound at the ankle. They were dubbed "bloomers" and were her personal protest against restrictions on women's attire. Dress reform and women's suffrage were her major concerns.
1881 : Notorious outlaw BILLY the KID (WILLIAM H. BONNEY)
was shot dead by Sheriff PAT GARRETT.
1891 : Golf caddies made their first appearance on the
course. It was the first game at the Royal Melbourne Golf Course in Caulfield. The first game of golf in Australia was reportedly played in Melbourne in 1847.
1934 : Polish-born scientist, MARIE CURIE, who discovered
radium, died. She won two Nobel Prizes, for Physics in 1903 and for Chemistry in 1911.
1935 : In Australia a packet of 333 brand cigarettes cost
sixpence.
1941 : The King approved a posthumous VC to Corporal J.H.
EDMONSON for gallantry at Tobruk. Corporal EDMONSON was the first Australian VC winner of World War II.
1943 : WLADYSLAW SIKORSKI, Polish statesman and prime
minister, was killed in an air crash. He led Poland's government in exile during World War Two.
1967 : An ACTU survey revealed that 750,000 Australians
were living in poverty, including 200,000 children under the age of 15.
1968 : In Melbourne 45 people were arrested during a

2,000-strong anti-Vietnam war demonstration outside the American Consulate. The following year, on American Independence day 1969, thousands of people marched in Canberra, Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide and Brisbane, in protest at the continuing war.
1976 : Israeli commandos rescued more than 100 hostages

held by pro-Palestinian hijackers at Entebbe airport. In the 35-minute battle 20 Ugandan soldiers, all seven terrorists, three hostages and one Israeli commando died. The rescue raid came only hours before the deadline set for killing the hostages. The hijackers had demanded the release of 53 Palestinian prisoners.
1986 : New York's Statue of Liberty was given a facelift.
The restoration project was to celebrate the statue's centenary.
1994 : French President FRANCOIS MITTERRAND became the
first foreigner to address South Africa's new parliament.
